question: Select the most appropriate option the fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is '**were**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses Mr. Cyril Boggis and his business. Since the description refers to his business in the past tense, the verb should align with that tense.
 
• The correct answer is "**were**" because it matches the past tense used throughout the passage and indicates that his premises were not large at that time.
 
• Other options like "are", "was", and "is" are incorrect as they do not match the past tense narrative of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *Apart from the fact that he was at this moment, disguised as a spiritual leader in the Christian Church, there was nothing sinister about Mr. Cyril Boggis. He was by trade a dealer in antique furniture, with his own shop and showroom in the King’s Road, Chelsea. His premises were__ not large, and generally he did not do a great deal of business, but because he always bought very, very cheap and sold very, very cheap he managed to make quite a tidy little income every year.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"Are" (हैं) **is used for present tense, which doesn't fit the past-tense context of the passage.
 
• **"Was" (था) **is a past-tense form but doesn't correctly match the plural subject "premises", which requires "were".
 
• **"Is" (है) **is used for present tense, which is not appropriate in this past-tense description of Mr. Boggis' business.
